svg:
Doppler: moving source compresses wavefronts ahead, stretches behind
<circle cx="150" cy="150" r="10" fill="none" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width:0.8"/> <circle cx="150" cy="150" r="25" fill="none" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width:0.8"/> <circle cx="150" cy="150" r="40" fill="none" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width:0.8"/> <circle cx="150" cy="150" r="55" fill="none" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width:0.8"/> Stationary source: λ same all directions
source v_s →
<circle cx="-30" cy="0" r="55" fill="none" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width:0.8"/> <circle cx="-20" cy="0" r="40" fill="none" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width:0.8"/> <circle cx="-10" cy="0" r="25" fill="none" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width:0.8"/> <circle cx="0" cy="0" r="10" fill="none" stroke="#1f5fa8" stroke-width:0.8"/>
Moving source: ahead λ' = (v - v_s)/f, behind λ' = (v + v_s)/f f' = f * v / (v ∓ v_s) [ - for approaching, + for receding, observer stationary ] Physical origin: wavelength in medium changes because source moves during emission. Valid: v_s < v, steady motion, point source
